hints: Focus on counting gases only, not solids or aqueous products, and remember what state each product is in at high temperature or room temperature.
Write out the thermal decomposition of calcium nitrate, it gives a solid oxide plus two different brown and colourless gases.
Compare that with carbonate decomposition and calcium with water, then check which of those give only one gas like carbon dioxide or hydrogen.
walkthrough:
**Recall what counts as a gaseous product**

We need two separate substances that are gases under the reaction conditions. Solids like $\text{CaO}$ and aqueous $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ do not count.

Rule to use:
$$\text{count gases} = \text{number of products with state (g)}$$

**Check reaction 1: heating calcium nitrate**

Group 2 nitrates decompose on heating to the oxide plus nitrogen dioxide plus oxygen. Both non-metal products are gases.

$$2\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2(s) \rightarrow 2\text{CaO}(s) + 4\text{NO}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g)$$
So reaction 1 gives two gaseous products and is correct.

**Check reaction 2: heating calcium carbonate**

Carbonates decompose to the oxide plus carbon dioxide only. That is just one gas.

$$\text{CaCO}_3(s) \rightarrow \text{CaO}(s) + \text{CO}_2(g)$$
So reaction 2 does not give two gases.

**Check reaction 3: calcium with water**

Calcium is reactive and gives calcium hydroxide plus hydrogen. Hydrogen is the only gas, the hydroxide stays in solution or as a solid.

$$\text{Ca}(s) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightarrow \text{Ca(OH)}_2(aq) + \text{H}_2(g)$$
So reaction 3 does not give two gases. Only 1 qualifies.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean all three give two gases. Reactions 2 and 3 each give only one gas, $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2$ respectively, so this overcounts.
options.B: Incorrect. While reaction 1 is correct, reaction 2 is often miscounted. $\text{CaCO}_3$ gives $\text{CaO}(s) + \text{CO}_2(g)$, only one gaseous product, not two.
options.C: Incorrect. Neither 2 nor 3 gives two gases. Students sometimes think $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ vapour or $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ is gaseous, but water is the liquid reactant and calcium hydroxide is aqueous or solid.
options.D: Correct. Only reaction 1 gives two gaseous products, $\text{NO}_2(g)$ and $\text{O}_2(g)$. Reactions 2 and 3 give only one gas each, so 1 only is the right combination.
